description: Evaluation cases for the cloud-engine-canisters skill. Tests whether agents apply the CloudEngine subnet call rules: never attach a cycles amount to calls they write (drop the `(with cycles = …)` clause rather than zeroing it) while keeping the schedule-aware management-canister wrappers, make cross-subnet calls bounded-wait, issue HTTPS outcalls directly from the engine canister instead of through the console proxy, and route cycle-requiring mainnet targets (XRC, threshold signing, vetKD) through the funded console proxy with the cycles inside ProxyArgs.

output_evals.name: Adversarial: unbounded-wait rejection from an engine subnet
output_evals.prompt: My Motoko canister runs on a cloud engine. Its call to a canister on another subnet is rejected with: "Unbounded-wait calls and calls with cycles are not allowed to CloudEngine subnets". What is wrong and what is the one-line fix to the call expression? No full code listing.
expected_behaviors: Identifies that plain awaits are unbounded-wait (guaranteed-response) calls, which the protocol rejects for cross-subnet messages from a CloudEngine subnet
Fixes it with a bounded-wait call using the Motoko parenthetical, e.g. `await (with timeout = N) service.method(args)`
Does NOT propose routing this cycle-less call through the console proxy canister, and does NOT suggest topping up the canister with cycles

output_evals.name: Adversarial: cycles attached on an engine, user proposes cycles = 0
output_evals.prompt: My canister on a cloud engine fails with IC0504 on a call written as `await (with cycles = 1_000_000_000) service.method(args)`. I was told engines hold 0 cycles, so I plan to change it to `with cycles = 0`. Is that the right fix? Answer briefly.
expected_behaviors: Says the fix is to remove the `(with cycles = …)` clause entirely rather than zeroing it — an engine call should not mention cycles at all
Explains nothing on an engine needs paying for — every fee is charged as zero under the engine's free cost schedule — so a cycles attachment is never needed
Gives the corrected call as a plain `await service.method(args)` (plus `with timeout` if the target is on another subnet)
Does NOT suggest topping up or funding the engine canister with cycles

output_evals.name: HTTPS outcall from an engine canister
output_evals.prompt: My Motoko canister runs on a cloud engine and needs to call an external REST API over HTTPS. Does the outcall code need anything engine-specific, and what about the cycles? Just the call line and a one-sentence note on cycles.
expected_behaviors: Says no engine-specific outcall form is needed — keeps the standard wrapper `Call.httpRequest(request)` from `mo:ic` (or notes `ic_cdk::management_canister::http_request` for Rust)
Explains the wrapper consults the cost API (`ic0.cost_http_request`), which is cost-schedule aware and returns 0 on an engine, so nothing is attached
Does NOT attach a hardcoded or hand-computed cycles amount, and does NOT tell the user to top up the engine canister
Does NOT route the outcall through the console proxy canister

output_evals.name: Adversarial: proxied outcall fails consensus
output_evals.prompt: From my cloud-engine canister I route HTTPS outcalls through the console proxy canister, and they fail with `SYS_TRANSIENT: No consensus could be reached. Replicas had different responses`. Why does this happen and what should I do instead? Briefly.
expected_behaviors: Explains the transform function must live on the canister that issues http_request — behind the proxy that is the proxy itself, which exposes no transform, so per-replica response differences are never normalized and consensus fails
Tells the user to issue the outcall directly from their own canister (free on an engine, no cycles attached), with the transform on that canister
Does NOT suggest retrying the proxied call or adding cycles

output_evals.name: Adversarial: proxied outcalls drain the proxy budget
output_evals.prompt: I'm bulk-importing ~4000 records into my cloud engine canister, each needing one HTTPS outcall to a vendor REST API. I route the outcalls through the engine's console proxy canister, and now every call fails with the proxy's InsufficientCycles (required ~72B per call). Should I ask for the proxy's budget to be raised? Answer briefly.
expected_behaviors: Says no — an HTTPS outcall does not belong on the proxy; issue it directly from the engine canister, where outcalls are free, so no budget exists to exhaust
Explains the proxy sits on a normal Application subnet and pays the real outcall fee from its funded balance, which a bulk workload drains
Does NOT recommend topping up the proxy or enabling auto top-up as the fix
Notes the direct outcalls need the transform on the calling canister, and/or `is_replicated = ?false`, to hold up at that volume

output_evals.name: Exchange rate canister through the console proxy
output_evals.prompt: My canister on a cloud engine needs an ICP/USD rate from the exchange rate canister (XRC), which lives on another subnet and charges cycles. How do I call it? Outline the mechanism and where the cycles go — no full code listing.
expected_behaviors: States the engine canister cannot call the XRC directly: cross-subnet calls from a CloudEngine subnet cannot carry cycles
Routes the call through the console proxy canister, deployed and funded from the engine console (Applications → Proxy canisters)
Puts the XRC fee inside `ProxyArgs.cycles` (the proxy attaches them locally), with candid-encoded target args passed as a blob
Does NOT attach cycles to the outer call to the proxy itself
